one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: India's largest industrial and logistics infrastructure developer, owner and operator in terms of Total Network area (Source: JLL Report), with a pan-India network of 45 assets across 10 cities totalling 58.58 msf as of the date of the RHP.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Horizon Industrial Parks develops, owns and operates Grade A fulfillment centers (warehouses), industrial facilities and in-city centers across India's major industrial and consumption hubs, offering built-to-suit and fully fitted plug-and-play space on lease. Around this core leasing business it wraps an integrated ecosystem of turnkey development/fit-out, rooftop solar energy solutions, cold storage, on-site staff accommodation and skill development centers, and an under-development hospitality offering. As of May 31, 2026 it served over 118 customers across e-commerce, third-party logistics, FMCG, retail, renewable energy, auto-ancillary and manufacturing, with an Operational Network of 28.55 msf at 93.56% Committed Occupancy. The Company is promoted by Blackstone entities (BREP), which acquired 100% of the then equity share capital in May 2021.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Vision Softech Facilities Private Limited — 49.00% stake acquired by the Company: Allotted a 100-acre land parcel in Narsapura, Bangalore with a potential of 2.55 msf; including it the total network is 46 assets / 61.13 msf
- Identified Subsidiaries (16 wholly owned subsidiaries whose borrowings are to be repaid from Net Proceeds) — Wholly owned Subsidiaries: Bagur Logistics Park Private Limited, Embassy Industrial Park Hosur Private Limited, Farukhnagar Logistics Parks LLP, FRK II Industrial Park Private Limited, Goodluck Buildtech Private Limited, ILV Distripark Private Limited, ILV Distripark (MWC) Private Limited, Jindpur Industrial Park Private Limited, Kalina Warehousing Private Limited, Lakshmipathi Realtors Private Limited, LI Industrial Parks Private Limited, Malur Logistics and Industrial Parks Private Limited, Panvel Warehousing Private Limited, Patencheru Industrial Park Private Limited, Redhills Industrial Park Private Limited and Vertical Logistic Park LLP
- Jazz Leaf Investment Limited and Embassy Property Developments Private Limited — Erstwhile Shareholders: Held 100% of the equity share capital until May 2021, when the Blackstone/BREP Promoters acquired 100.00% of the then equity share capital
- Group Company — Group Company as defined under Regulation 2(1)(t) of the SEBI ICDR Regulations: The Board adopted the group-company identification policy by resolution dated July 23, 2026, but the name(s) of the identified Group Company are cut off in the provided extract; the RHP states there is no pending litigation involving the Group Company that may have a material impact on the Company
- Other subsidiaries in which directors hold board seats — Subsidiaries / affiliated entities named via directorships of Urvish Jayantilal Rambhia and Alok Kumar Jain: Includes Banamakanahalli Industrial and Logistics Private Limited, Juturna Developers Private Limited, XSIO Industrial Parks Private Limited, Bhiwandi Industrial and Logistics Parks Private Limited, Talegaon Industrial Parks Private Limited, Volumnus Developers Private Limited, Kothur Logistics Park Private Limited, Orbitex Induspark Private Limited and Headway Logistix Induspark Private Limited; the RHP extract lists these as directorships and does not itself label each as a subsidiary

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Fulfillment centers (warehouses):** Bulk storage solutions for e-commerce, third-party logistics, FMCG and retail customers, 16.34 msf of Operational Network as of May 31, 2026 (57.23% of total Operational Network), Committed Occupancy 91.58% as of May 31, 2026, Facility sizes typically 50,000 sq ft to over 500,000 sq ft; clear heights of around 12 metres, floors with 5-8 tonnage loads, 16m wide concrete docking-apron, 12-metre turning radius
- **Industrial facilities:** Space for assembly, light engineering, manufacturing and associated storage — renewable energy, EV, automotive, electronics, aerospace, specialty chemicals, telecom and packaging, 11.42 msf of Operational Network as of May 31, 2026 (40.00% of total Operational Network), Committed Occupancy 95.94% as of May 31, 2026, Plug-and-play plus built-to-suit; footprints typically 50,000 sq ft to 800,000 sq ft with wide column spans, RHP states industrial facilities offer attractive yields and foster customer stickiness
- **In-city centers:** Multi-use facilities near dense residential clusters — last-mile delivery stations, micro fulfillment centers, dark stores, D2C, online pharma, cold storage, cloud kitchens, service centers, airline catering, online laundry, experience centers, large format retail, R&D centers and SME industrial facilities, Three operational facilities with 0.79 msf of Operational Network and 100.00% Committed Occupancy as of May 31, 2026, Total Network of in-city centers of 6.91 msf across seven cities as of the RHP date; 14 additional facilities at various stages of development
- **Integrated ecosystem offerings (ancillary revenue streams):** Turnkey Solutions — capital expenditure and fit-out solutions for select customers with demonstrated credit quality and long-term commitments, Energy Solutions — rooftop solar; total operational capacity 21.31 MW as of May 31, 2026, with a further 17.20 MW being installed, On-site staff accommodation and skill development centers (the latter in partnership with the Confederation of Indian Industry), Cold storage across ambient, chilled and frozen temperature ranges, developed with in-house execution expertise, Hospitality — under development as of the RHP date; a 115-key on-campus mid-scale hotel is under construction at Horizon Industrial Park Dobbaspet I, Bangalore

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Vertical integration is the stated core of the model: the management team and the assets are housed under a single corporate structure rather than the traditional fragmented development-manager/operating model, which the RHP states removes management-fee leakage and manager-owner conflict and speeds decision-making. It describes itself as the only scaled pure-play industrial and logistics platform combining real estate, infrastructure and operational services under one roof (Source: JLL Report). Downstream of the shell, the Company bundles an ecosystem into the same customer relationship: turnkey development with capital-expenditure and fit-out solutions for select customers with demonstrated credit quality and long-term commitments (stated to enhance overall realization), rooftop solar energy solutions monetizing its own roof footprint (21.31 MW operational, 17.20 MW being installed), on-site staff accommodation and CII-partnered skill development centers, cold storage developed with in-house execution expertise, racking and material handling equipment, and an under-development hospitality offering. In-house engineering and technical capability supports execution of complex industrial projects to Grade A+ specifications with cost discipline. Upstream, the network was assembled through acquisitions (32 of 45 assets, 62.00% of Total Network, from Promoters and their related entities), greenfield development and strategic redevelopment, alongside joint ventures and government partnerships. The RHP states this compresses customer time-to-market to approximately six to nine months versus the typical 24 to 30 months when a customer manages all aspects independently (Source: JLL Report).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- IMPORTANT — the MD&A section in the routed extract contains only the introductory basis-of-preparation preamble; no discussion of revenue, cost, margin or working-capital drivers was included in the extract provided, so the items below are drawn from the Our Business and Objects sections rather than from MD&A itself
- All financial information in the Business/MD&A sections is presented on a PROFORMA basis, illustrating the Acquisition Transactions as if implemented from April 1, 2023 or the date of incorporation of the relevant entity, whichever is later — comparability with future reported results is explicitly disclaimed by the Company
- Revenue growth is a function of Operational Network additions (20.70 to 23.31 to 28.42 msf across FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026, and 28.55 msf at May 31, 2026) multiplied by Committed Occupancy, which was 92.01% FY2024, 93.94% FY2025, 89.88% FY2026 and 93.56% at May 31, 2026 — the FY2026 dip reflects newly delivered area entering the denominator ahead of lease-up
- Mix shift toward industrial facilities is a stated yield lever — the Company says industrial facilities offer attractive yields and foster customer stickiness; they were 40.00% of the Operational Network at May 31, 2026
- Ancillary ecosystem revenue (turnkey fit-outs, energy solutions, cold storage, accommodation, hospitality) is described as contributing directly to revenue streams, with turnkey work enhancing overall realization and solar being accretive to overall yields
- Customer retention economics — 40.65% of incremental area contracted since Fiscal 2024 came from repeat engagements, and the customer count rose 79 to 95 to 114 to 118 across FY2024, FY2025, FY2026 and May 31, 2026
- Capital structure — the Company is applying Rs 22,500.00 million of Issue proceeds to repay/prepay borrowings of itself and 16 Identified Subsidiaries, so interest cost is a material P&L line whose reduction is an explicit post-listing driver
- Pre-leasing of the development pipeline (2.57 msf pre-contracted across eight locations at May 31, 2026) determines how quickly delivered area converts into rental revenue

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Deliver the 30.03 msf Development Network (7.22 msf Near Term Deliveries plus 22.81 msf Planned Projects) over the next four to five years to capture forecast Grade A stock growth
- Scale the in-city centers vertical — three facilities operational (0.79 msf) with 14 additional facilities at various stages of development across key metropolitan areas and a 6.91 msf in-city Total Network across seven cities
- Grow through the same three channels used to date: strategic acquisitions, greenfield development of barren land into commercial hubs, and targeted strategic redevelopments
- Deepen the integrated ecosystem to raise realisation and stickiness — turnkey capex/fit-out solutions for select credit-worthy, long-tenure customers; cold storage using in-house execution expertise
- Expand rooftop solar energy solutions from 21.31 MW operational capacity with a further 17.20 MW being installed, positioned as accretive to overall yields
- Build out on-site staff accommodation (four upcoming facilities, potential for over 2,000 beds in Chennai, Bangalore, Pune and Delhi-NCR) and CII-partnered skill development centers to supply customers with trained labour
- Enter hospitality — develop hotels in locations with a concentration of industrial customers and significant white-collar employee bases, starting with a 115-key on-campus mid-scale hotel at Dobbaspet I, Bangalore
- Deleverage the balance sheet by applying the Net Proceeds to repay/prepay borrowings of the Company and 16 Identified Subsidiaries
- Note: a dedicated 'Our Strategies' sub-section was not included in the routed extract; the intents above are drawn from stated plans in the Our Business, Objects of the Issue and History sections

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The growth engine is the 30.03 msf Development Network held within the existing fence, split between 7.22 msf of Near Term Deliveries (projects under active development with pre-construction approvals obtained) and 22.81 msf of Planned Projects (land or development rights secured, approvals possibly still pending, with on-site development or initial planning underway). The Company states this pipeline is expected to be delivered over the next four to five years and is positioned to capture the market growth the JLL Report forecasts. Development is concentrated in the same 10 industrial and consumption hubs, with the in-city vertical the most aggressive push — three operating facilities today versus 14 more under development, and a 6.91 msf in-city Total Network across seven cities. Inorganic and JV expansion continues alongside: a 49.00% stake was acquired in Vision Softech Facilities Private Limited, which holds a 100-acre Narsapura (Bangalore) parcel with 2.55 msf potential, lifting the network to 46 assets and 61.13 msf. Ancillary capacity is expanding in parallel — rooftop solar from 21.31 MW operational with 17.20 MW under installation; four additional staff accommodation facilities with potential for over 2,000 beds in Chennai, Bangalore, Pune and Delhi-NCR; a first 115-key hotel under construction at Dobbaspet I, Bangalore; and CII-partnered skill development centers. Demand visibility for the pipeline is partly locked: 2.57 msf was pre-contracted across eight locations as of May 31, 2026. Historically the build-out has been acquisition-led — the Company held five assets before the May 2021 Blackstone change of control and the other 40 assets were acquired thereafter, with a significant portion bought from the Promoters and other sellers in Fiscals 2025 and 2026.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Largest industrial and logistics infrastructure developer, owner and operator in India in terms of Total Network area (Source: JLL Report) — 45 assets, 58.58 msf across 10 cities as of the RHP date
- Pan-India footprint concentrated in the major industrial and consumption hubs — Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bangalore, Chennai, Pune, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad and Nagpur among 10 cities
- Fully integrated end-to-end ecosystem — turnkey development and fit-outs, rooftop solar, cold storage, on-site staff accommodation, skill development centers and (under development) hospitality — which the Company says fosters stickiness and is accretive to overall yields
- Marquee customer base — over 118 customers as of May 31, 2026, with 54.05% of the committed Operational Network contracted to Fortune 500 companies
- Demonstrated customer stickiness — 40.65% of incremental area contracted since Fiscal 2024 was signed through repeated engagements
- High and improving utilisation — Committed Occupancy of 93.56% at May 31, 2026 across 28.55 msf of Operational Network (91.58% fulfillment centers, 95.94% industrial facilities, 100.00% in-city centers)
- Speed to market — the offering is designed to enable customer production within approximately six to nine months versus the typical 24 to 30 months of managing all aspects independently (Source: JLL Report)
- Blackstone sponsorship — Promoters are part of the Blackstone Group, whose global logistics holdings exceeded 1.2 billion sq ft as of September 30, 2025; network growth accelerated after the May 2021 change in control (five assets pre-May 2021 versus 45 today)
- Large embedded growth pipeline already secured — 30.03 msf Development Network within the fence, of which 2.57 msf was pre-contracted to customers across eight locations as of May 31, 2026

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Recently acquired asset base bought largely from the Promoters, with only illustrative proforma financials to judge it by — A significant portion of the network was acquired from the Promoters and other sellers in Fiscals 2025 and 2026 — before Fiscal 2025 the Total Network comprised only ten assets versus 45 today. The Proforma Financial Information assumes those acquisitions were consummated on April 1, 2023 (or the entity's incorporation date, if later) and the RHP expressly warns it may not accurately reflect the Company's financial condition or results of operations. This is the RHP's own first-ranked risk factor (risks are ordered by materiality) and it is simultaneously a related-party concentration risk.
- Execution and capital intensity of a 30.03 msf development pipeline — 22.81 msf of the pipeline sits in 'Planned Projects', where the RHP's own definition concedes that pre-construction approvals 'may or may not have been obtained from the relevant authorities' and where activity may be no more than initial planning and design. Delivery is promised over four to five years; slippage in approvals, land or construction directly defers the revenue that justifies the valuation.
- Occupancy and lease-up lag on newly delivered area — Committed Occupancy fell from 93.94% at March 31, 2025 to 89.88% at March 31, 2026 as the Operational Network grew from 23.31 to 28.42 msf, before recovering to 93.56% at May 31, 2026. Each delivery wave re-opens this gap between built area and contracted area.
- Customer and tenant concentration — Only 118 customers occupy 28.55 msf, and 54.05% of the committed Operational Network is contracted to Fortune 500 companies (including end tenants of 3PL clients). The loss or downsizing of a small number of large tenants would move occupancy and rental revenue materially. The RHP does not disclose a top-10 customer revenue share in the provided extract.
- Leverage and dependence on the Issue to deleverage — Rs 22,500.00 million of the Rs 26,000.00 million Gross Proceeds — roughly 87% — is earmarked for repaying or prepaying borrowings of the Company and 16 wholly owned Identified Subsidiaries, leaving little primary capital for growth. Development of the remaining pipeline must therefore be funded from operations or fresh debt.
- Geographic and asset-class concentration in a single real-asset cycle — The whole network sits in 10 Indian cities and in one asset class — industrial and logistics real estate — whose demand is levered to e-commerce, 3PL and manufacturing capex. There is no diversification across geographies outside India or across property types beyond the nascent in-city, cold storage and hospitality verticals.
- Reliance on a commissioned industry report for the Company's headline positioning claims — The RHP itself carries a risk factor titled 'Certain sections of this Red Herring Prospectus contain information from the JLL Report which has been exclusively commissioned and paid for by our Company in relation to the Issue and any reliance on such information contained therein for making an investment decision in this offering is subject to inherent risks'. The 'India's largest' claim, the 25.3% CAGR / 943.6 msf CY2030 market forecast and the six-to-nine-month time-to-market comparison all rest on that paid-for JLL Report dated July 23, 2026.
- Financial-statement comparability under Ind AS and the proforma presentation — The RHP carries a risk factor titled 'Significant differences exist between Ind AS and other accounting principles, such as IFRS and U.S. GAAP, which may be material to investors' assessments of our financial condition' (page 74), on top of the proforma presentation basis. Investors are being asked to underwrite a track record that the issuer itself labels illustrative.
- Extract caveat — the routed slice contains only risk factor 1 and the section preamble — The full risk-factor list was not included in the text provided to this task; the structural risks above are inferred from the business, objects and litigation sections plus the two risk-factor titles quoted by cross-reference. This is not an assertion that the RHP discloses no other risks.
